purpose: To calculate and detail the prolongation charges for the Construction of Extension to Assembly Integration and Test Facility (AITF-1) due to project delays.
summary: This document details the calculation of prolongation charges for M/s. It calculates a total prolongation charge of 1,81,66,196.60 based on 173 balance delay days, after accounting for a 310-day Covid period from a total of 483 delay days. The calculation uses a daily prolongation charge rate of 1,05,006.92, derived from the initial WO Value of 1,26,00,83,001.00 and a 7.5% prolongation charge factor.

Despite multiple previous communications, the work is progressing very slowly, with many critical activities either incomplete or not yet commenced, falling far behind revised target dates. The document details specific delays in Block-1&1A and Block-2, attributing all delays to URC Construction. The letter urges the contractor to take immediate action to improve progress and meet the stipulated milestones.

It responds to the contractor's letter and rejects their stated reasons for delay, such as festivals, Lok Sabha elections, Cyclone Fani, and water non-availability, deeming them unacceptable. ISRO attributes the delays solely to URC Construction and requests immediate action to improve progress and meet agreement milestones.

purpose: To inform M/s URC Construction (P) Limited about specific issues observed at the construction site for the AITF-I extension project and request immediate action to ensure quality assurance.
parties: ISRO Satellite Centre (Government of India, Department of Space)
summary: This letter from ISRO Satellite Centre to M/s URC Construction (P) Limited addresses several issues observed at the construction site for the AITF-I extension project. Key concerns include improper protection of rebar threads, inadequate backfilling and compaction of earth in foundation pits, and failure to mark casting dates on structural members. Additionally, the letter requests the immediate submission of manufactured test certificates for materials like anti-termite treatment and anti-corrosive paints. URC Construction is urged to promptly address these points to ensure quality assurance at the site.

While concrete work for two footings is complete, further excavation for balance footings is stalled. This delay is attributed to waterlogging caused by an adjacent agency's work, making the soil moist and unsuitable for further excavation.

It highlights that the work, awarded with a 30-month construction period, is significantly behind schedule, with daily labor strength being insufficient. The document lists the current minimal progress compared to the first milestone scheduled for 17.01.2019. ISRO requests the contractor to take immediate action to expedite the work by deploying sufficient construction workers and materials to meet the milestones.

Rao Satellite Centre (URSC), which levied compensation for a 68-day delay and only considered 75 days for price escalation against their claim for 483 days. URC argues that URSC's levy is belated, contrary to contract provisions (Clause 5.4 GCC), and disregards prior discussions where the Director agreed to an Extension of Time until 15.05.2022 without compensation. URC asserts that no delay is attributable to them and requests URSC to review and recall the levy letter, subsequently releasing the entire final bill amount along with the final escalation bill.

They detail expenses incurred for idle workforce, machinery, and other incidentals, citing government orders that mandate wage payments during the lockdown. Despite previous rejections of their claims, URC emphasizes that these unanticipated costs were not part of the original contract. They request reimbursement to alleviate financial strain and ensure the project's completion, promising to provide actual expenditure details once the situation normalizes.

purpose: This document is a formal request from URC Construction (P) Ltd to U.R Rao Satellite Centre to permit the supply of materials and resume construction work, proposing a payment adjustment to mitigate financial strain.

summary: URC Construction (P) Ltd, the contractor for the "Construction of Extension to AITF-1 at ISITE, Marathahalli, Bangalore," informs U.R Rao Satellite Centre that 60% of the project was completed before the March 2020 COVID-19 lockdown. Major specialized materials were ordered and ready for dispatch in March 2020 but were put on hold when ISRO suspended work. Despite government relaxations and repeated requests, URC has not received permission to resume work. Vendors are now pressuring URC for delivery and payments, causing financial strain and interest expenses on unadjusted mobilization advance. URC requests intervention to permit material supply and project commencement, proposing to adjust payments against mobilization advance to avoid cash flow loss for ISRO.

summary:
This document is a reply from Kumar M.N., advocate for the Union of India/ISRO, to a demand notice from Shri Abhilash Raju V., advocate for M/s. URC Constructions (P) Ltd. The reply addresses the construction of an extension to the Assembly Integration and Test facility (AITF-1) at ISITE, Bangalore, detailing the tender process and the awarded contract amount of ₹1,26,00,83,001/-.
It extensively chronicles communications between ISRO and URC Constructions from July 2018 to February 2019, highlighting URC's alleged delays in submitting mandatory documents, deploying key personnel, and achieving milestones. The document also notes ISRO's various approvals, reminders, and rejections of URC's claims regarding hindrances. The reply aims to present a chronological account of events, asserting that URC Constructions has suppressed details and selectively referred to communications in their demand notice.

purpose: To formally invoke Clause 25 of the General Conditions of Contract (GCC) for arbitration to settle outstanding claims and disputes related to a construction project, including withheld payments and levied liquidated damages.
parties: The Group Head, Construction and Maintenance Group, Department of Space, U.R.RAO Satellite Centre
summary: This letter from URC Construction (P) Ltd to the Department of Space, dated 27.09.2024, formally invokes Clause 25 of the GCC to settle claims related to the AITF-1 construction project. URC details a history of project delays, extensions of time, and financial losses due to COVID-19 shutdowns and the department's alleged arbitrary levy of liquidated damages and non-payment of certified amounts. Despite earlier recommendations for EOT and certified payments, the Engineer-in-Charge rejected claims, prompting URC to file a writ petition. URC seeks arbitration for balance escalation payments, reversal of liquidated damages, and compensation for COVID-19 expenses, prolongation costs, and interest.

purpose: To notify M/s URC Construction (P) Limited about the slow progress and delay in construction works, attribute the delay to them, and request immediate action to meet the first milestone as per the agreement, warning of potential contractual actions.

summary: This document is a notice from ISRO Satellite Centre to M/s URC Construction (P) Limited, dated 07.12.2018, addressing the slow progress and delay in the construction of the Extension to Assembly Integration & Test facility (AITF-1). It references previous communications and highlights that work is not aligning with the agreed milestones, specifically the first milestone due by 17.01.2019. The notice details specific activities that have slipped from their schedule, notes a lack of concreting for 9 days, and insufficient labor deployment. It attributes the delays entirely to URC Construction and requests immediate action to improve progress and meet the milestone, warning of potential contractual actions if the situation does not improve.

summary: URC Construction (P) Ltd issued a notice to the Engineer-in-Charge regarding the severe impact of the COVID-19 pandemic and the subsequent government-imposed lockdown on their construction project, 'Extension to Assembly Integration and Test Facility (AITF 1)'. Concurrently, URC Construction's emails urgently request an appointment with ISRO's Member (Finance) to expedite the release of a Rs. 13.21 Crores final bill and escalation payment, citing severe financial distress due to the two-year delay since project completion.

summary: URC Construction (P) Ltd issues a formal notice to the Director of ISRO Satellite Centre (ISAC) expressing non-acceptance of their final decision regarding claims and extension of time for the AITF-1 construction project. URC contends that the Director's decision, communicated via a Senior Administrative Officer, lacks detailed reasoning, contradicts contractual terms, and disregards previous recommendations for Extension of Time (EOT) without Liquidated Damages (LD). URC highlights several points of disagreement, including the authority for EOT approval, failure to consider delay analysis, and non-application of relevant clauses. Consequently, URC informs ISAC of its intention to refer the entire claims to a Court of Law as per Clause 25 of the contract agreement.

purpose: To provide a point-wise reply to queries raised by M/s URC Construction (P) Ltd regarding the final extension of time, compensation, and price escalation for the AITF-1 construction project.
summary: This document is a reply from U.R. Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) to M/s URC Construction (P) Limited, addressing queries regarding the final extension of time (EOT), compensation, and price escalation for the AITF-1 construction project. URSC reiterates its decision to grant 415 days of justified delay and attribute 68 unjustified days to the contractor, leading to compensation. It clarifies that price escalation is limited to the contract period plus 75 days, not the contractor's claimed 483 days, based on agreement conditions and competent authority approval. URSC also addresses URC's concerns about delayed EOT processing and the final bill, stating that the final bill and escalation will be settled according to the approved EOT.

purpose: This document levies compensation on M/s URC Construction (P) Limited for an unjustified delay in a construction project.
summary: This document, issued by the U.R. RAO Satellite Centre, Department of Space, Government of India, to M/s URC Construction (P) Limited, levies a compensation of 59,97,813.00. The compensation is for an unjustified delay of 68 days, from 09/03/2022 to 15/05/2022, in the construction of the Extension to Assembly Integration & Test facility (AITF-1). M/s URC Construction (P) Limited is required to pay this amount within one month, failing which it will be adjusted against other sums payable by the Government.

Rao Satellite Centre (URSC) to M/s URC Construction (P) Limited responds to the contractor's request not to levy compensation for delays in the AITF-1 construction project.
